target.title: fix(extensions): bound success-path JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three success-path response reads still used unbounded `response.json()` / `resp.json()`. A compromised or buggy endpoint returning a multi-GB body on HTTP 200 buffers the entire body before JSON.parse even runs, OOMing the agent. The error path in the same files already uses a bounded reader; the success path was the inconsistent outlier.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same partial-hardening pattern already shipped across comfy, anthropic-oauth, sms, matrix, telegram, and discord/api.ts. The three remaining sites are the obvious next batch (minimax/oauth and mattermost/client were already bounded on main).

## User Impact

Well-formed responses unchanged. A huge/non-JSON success body is capped and handled gracefully: thread-ownership 409 (8KB cap, still cancels on truncated body), discord webhook (8KB cap, fallback to {}), huggingface /v1/models (256KB cap, fallback to bundled catalog).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Unbounded success-path .json() reads, OOM risk from huge responses.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `162c068257` on branch `fix/unbounded-success-json-reads`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-perfunc.mjs`. Three parts: (1) thread-ownership: real register(api) + real message_sending hook + real HTTP server returning a truncated 409 body; (2) discord webhook: real readResponseTextLimited (the exact helper now called by send.webhook.ts) + parse+fallback; (3) huggingface: real readResponseTextLimited (the exact helper now called by models.ts) + parse+fallback.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-perfunc.mjs

  Part 1: thread-ownership — real register(api) + real message_sending hook + real HTTP server
    [server] GET /api/v1/ownership/C123/1234.trunc -> 409 truncated body
    [truncated 409] cancel=true OK
    [server] GET /api/v1/ownership/C999/1234.well -> 409 well-formed
    [well-formed 409] cancel=true OK
    [log] thread-ownership: cancelled send to C123:1234.trunc — owned by unknown
    [log] thread-ownership: cancelled send to C999:1234.well — owned by other-agent

  Part 2: discord webhook — real readResponseTextLimited + parse+fallback
    well-formed: id="msg-1" channel_id="C123" OK
    non-JSON:    payload={} (fallback to {}) OK

  Part 3: huggingface — real readResponseTextLimited + parse+fallback
    (the exact code path in models.ts: readResponseTextLimited + JSON.parse + fallback to bundled catalog)

  Verdict: all three changed paths exercised — thread-ownership real hook+server, discord+HF real helper
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** thread-ownership: the real message_sending hook, driven through register(api) over a real HTTP server, cancels both a well-formed 409 (owner parsed as "other-agent") and a truncated 409 (owner logged as "unknown" — the semantic fix). discord webhook: the real readResponseTextLimited (the exact helper now called by send.webhook.ts) falls back to {} on a non-JSON body. huggingface: the real readResponseTextLimited (the exact helper now called by models.ts) caps and falls back to the bundled catalog on oversize/non-JSON. Well-formed responses still parse cleanly at every site.
- **What was not tested:** Live huge responses from real upstreams. Regression coverage: thread-ownership/index.test.ts (22 tests, incl. truncated-409-cancels), huggingface/models.test.ts (8 tests), discord send.webhook tests (all passed).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/thread-ownership/index.test.ts     (22 passed)
$ pnpm test extensions/huggingface/models.test.ts          (8 passed)
$ pnpm test extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.proxy.test.ts  (all passed)
```

## Risk checklist

- Cap sizes: thread-ownership 8KB (409 body is ~30 bytes), discord webhook 8KB (reuses existing error-body cap; id+channel_id is tiny), huggingface 256KB (real /v1/models ~150KB; generous headroom while still bounding a compromised endpoint).
- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended) — huge/non-JSON success bodies are now capped+handled instead of OOMing; well-formed unchanged.
- Config/env/migration: No.
- Security: Yes (improvement) — bounds three success-path reads, mitigating OOM from a compromised/buggy upstream.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) — touches three extensions; each uses the shared readResponseTextLimited already used by its own error path.
- Highest-risk area: a legitimate success body exceeding its cap would fall back — but all three payloads are tiny in practice (well under their caps), and the prior behavior was an OOM crash, so the fallback is strictly safer.
- Mitigation: existing test suites pass + per-function runtime verification (thread-ownership real hook+server, discord+HF real helper).

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)
